intro.text: The alphabet of the Vorin nations, in which only women may read and write.

description.text: Women's script is a phonetic alphabet written left to right from the top-left of the page. Each letter is set by its shape and size, and can be changed by one or two small lines after it.
It has only one known punctuation mark, a vertical line with short crossbars at each end, written at the start of a sentence to set the letter height. Questions end with "ha".
It goes back at least 1,800 years, to an older form called the protoscript.
